A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Singleton-Optimized Conformal Prediction by the same authors. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on ImageNet-Val, ImageNet-V2, TissueMNIST, and MMLU, including benchmark comparisons and regularization analyses in Section 3 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds ImageNet size-stratified coverage results in Section 3.1.2 and newly reported empty-set frequencies.

M1.justification: The singleton-plus-size objective, nonconformity score, convex-hull computation, split-conformal procedure, and top-k extension are unchanged. Algorithms 1–3 retain their steps; the additional tuning objective is an experimental setting.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ImageNet-Val, ImageNet-V2, TissueMNIST, and MMLU coverage. The new adaptiveness analysis uses existing ImageNet-Val data and models without introducing a different task, population, or input environment.

E2.justification: Plug-In, RAPS, Pure Singleton, Least Ambiguous Sets, and the separately reported CPL comparison are retained. New Table 2 uses the same comparator set as Table 1; SSCV-specific tuning changes settings rather than comparator membership.

E3.justification: New Section 3.1.2 evaluates size-stratified coverage violation (SSCV) using strata 0–1, 2–3, 4–10, 11–100, and 101–1000, selecting RAPS and SOCOP regularization to minimize SSCV. This supplements the retained evaluation protocols; newly documented grids for existing experiments do not establish that those settings changed.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused adaptiveness analysis for ResNet152-v2 and ViT-h-14 on ImageNet-Val, examining coverage violations across prediction-set sizes. It also newly reports an empty-set check across experiments. Existing regularization sensitivity analyses and set-size histograms remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages and standard errors over 100 random splits. New Table 2 follows the existing protocol and uncertainty presentation; no increased repeat count, new seed policy, confidence interval, or significance-testing procedure is stated.

E6.justification: All original numerical table rows are retained. New Table 2 reports SOCOP/RAPS SSCV values of 0.039/0.031 for ResNet152-v2 and 0.041/0.047 for ViT-h-14 under SSCV-oriented tuning, alongside coverage and efficiency results. A new footnote reports empty sets below 0.01% except RAPS, reaching approximately 0.1%. These are additional findings, not improvements to matched earlier scores.

T1.justification: The definitions, optimization derivations, convex-hull theorem, limiting cases, and appendix proofs are substantively unchanged. v1's nested-sets Lemma B.1 becomes v2's Lemma 2.2 in the main text; its proof is retained. The new SSCV evaluation introduces no new theorem or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and concluding summary retain the same claims: a singleton-oriented score, efficient geometric computation, marginal coverage, and favorable singleton-frequency versus set-size tradeoffs. Added diagnostics and future directions do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explains why rare empty sets make its objective approximate maximizing exact singleton frequency and interprets the new SSCV results as supporting adaptiveness with relatively small sets. It also explains ImageNet-V2's natural distribution shift and discusses conditional-coverage-oriented objectives and tuning bias when reusing calibration data.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability link in the introduction and Appendix E specifying RAPS and SOCOP tuning grids, including separate efficiency and SSCV grids. The efficiency grids provide previously missing implementation details, without establishing changes to the original experiments. The linked resource's contents are not verified by the PDFs.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds a substantive distinction between deriving scores from a loss and selecting among candidate scores. New references include Gibbs et al., Yang and Kuchibhotla, and Zeng et al. The additional Liang 2024 entry shares the arXiv identifier of the Liang 2025 work already cited in v1.

P1.justification: v2 adds an adaptiveness subsection, a hyperparameter appendix, explanatory footnotes, and a geometric price interpretation. It moves the nested-sets lemma into the main text and corrects proof headings and references. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 2 with an SSCV column and separate model groups. Existing figures, algorithms, and tables retain their substantive displays but move with text reflow; subsequent tables and associated references are renumbered. There is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The added SSCV comparison tests an aspect of coverage absent from v1's evaluation, while the empty-set findings support the singleton interpretation. Explicit tuning grids and a code-access pointer improve reproducibility information. These are useful, focused gains: the new comparison uses separately tuned settings, and the method, proofs, and original benchmark results remain unchanged.
